name: People & Relationships
blurb: Six person-based cue cards. A single well-developed character can be adapted across most of them.

items: How did you learn to be polite as a child?
Do you think being polite is very important?
Who taught you to be polite when you were young?
Do you know your neighbours?
What do you think of your neighbours?
How do you get along with your neighbours?
Do you often see your neighbours?
Do you like watching movies that make you laugh?
Do you find it easy to make others laugh?
Do you think it is a good thing if you always make others laugh?
Do you have a favourite teacher?
Do you still keep in touch with your teachers?
What qualities should a good teacher have?

p2.t: Describe a person you only met once recently and want to know more about
b: Who he or she is
When you met him or her
Why you want to know more about him or her
And explain how you feel about him or her

p2.t: Describe a famous person in your local area
b: Who this person is
What he or she has done
Why he or she is popular
And explain how you feel about this person

p2.t: Describe a person you know who really likes taking photos
b: Who this person is
What he or she takes photos of
How often he or she takes photos
And explain how you feel about this person

p2.t: Describe a time when you interviewed a famous person
b: Who the famous person was
When and where you interviewed this person
What you talked about
And explain how you feel about the experience

p2.t: Describe a happy person you know
b: Who this person is
What he or she is like
How he or she shows happiness
And explain why you think he or she is a happy person

p2.t: Describe someone older than you that you admire
b: Who this person is
How you knew this person
What kinds of things you like to do together
And explain how you feel about this person

p2.t: Describe a friend from your childhood
b: Who he or she is
Where and how you met
What you often did together
And explain what made you like him or her

items: What can we do to leave a good impression on people we meet for the first time?
What should we not talk about when we meet someone for the first time?
How do people make friends in your country?
On what occasions do people like to make friends?
Is it important to have the same hobbies when making friends?
What qualities make true friends?
Do you still keep in touch with friends from childhood? Why or why not?
How important is childhood friendship to children?
Do you think online social media will replace face-to-face communication?
What can young and old people learn from each other?
Has older people's quality of life improved compared to the past?
Why is there a generation gap between the young and the old?
What do older people usually do in their daily life?
What kinds of people are usually interviewed?
Why do some people dislike being interviewed?
Why do some people think interviews are a waste of time?
What should people do to prepare for a job interview?
Is it always good to be a popular student at school?
Why are some students popular?
When do you think people are happiest?
Do you think teachers are able to spot unhappy children?
How can the arts spread positive emotions in society?
